summary: To wait on someone as his attendant, and above all to minister in Yahweh's worship. Joseph attends Potiphar, Joshua is “the minister of Moses”, Elisha goes after Elijah and serves him, and the king's attendants stand before him; the priests are chosen “to stand before Yahweh to minister to him and to bless in his name”, the Levites serve the tabernacle, the priests and the congregation, and there are garments and vessels “for ministering in the holy place”. Yahweh's angels are “his ministers who do his will”, and the restored Zion is promised a people called “priests of Yahweh, ministers of our God”. Outside Hebrew the root is known in Phoenician and Punic, where it is to serve a god and the community.

words.gloss: serve, attend, wait on; minister (in worship)
words.summary: Ninety-seven times, all in the piel. The one served is always a person: a master, a king, a prophet, Yahweh himself, the tabernacle or house as his dwelling, or the congregation; only twice is it idols (Ezk 20:32; 44:12). The participle מְשָׁרֵת is used as a noun, “attendant, minister”. It is service in someone's presence, standing before him, not the labour of a slave (עָבַד), and it is never used of Israel's bondage in Egypt.

stems.gloss: serve, attend on; minister before Yahweh; (participle) attendant, minister

senses.gloss: attend on, wait on (a master or king)
senses.definition: To be a man's personal attendant: to stay at his side and see to his needs and his business. The participle מְשָׁרֵת is the attendant himself, a young man who goes with his master and may succeed him (Joshua after Moses, Elisha after Elijah).

evidence.note: Joseph “found favour in his eyes, וַיְשָׁרֶת אֹתוֹ”, and Potiphar set him over his house: personal service that leads to trust.
The captain of the guard appointed Joseph to the butler and the baker, “and he served them”.
“His minister (מְשָׁרְתוֹ) Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from the tent.”
“Moses rose up, and Joshua his minister.”
“Joshua the son of Nun, the minister of Moses from his youth.”
After Moses' death Yahweh speaks to “Joshua the son of Nun, the minister of Moses”, who now takes his place.
Elisha “arose and went after Elijah and served him (וַיְשָׁרְתֵהוּ)”.
Elisha's attendant (מְשָׁרְתוֹ) doubts that twenty loaves will feed a hundred men.
“The attendant of the man of God rose early.”
Abishag “became to the king a companion, and served him (וַתְּשָׁרְתֵהוּ), but the king did not know her”.
Amnon calls “his young man who attended him (מְשָׁרְתוֹ)”.
The queen of Sheba sees “the attendance (מַעֲמַד) of his servants and the standing of his ministers (מְשָׁרְתָיו)”.
The seven eunuchs “who served before King Ahasuerus”.
“A ruler who listens to a word of falsehood, all his ministers are wicked.”
The king's rule for his household: “he who walks in a perfect way, he shall serve me (יְשָׁרְתֵנִי)”.
The divisions “who served the king in every matter of the divisions”.
“These were those serving the king.”
Jehu finds the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers “serving Ahaziah”.
Of Zion restored: “the sons of foreigners shall build your walls, and their kings shall serve you (יְשָׁרְתוּנֶךְ)”.

senses.definition: The priests' service in Yahweh's presence: to stand before him, draw near to the altar and enter the holy place, offer, burn incense and bless in his name. It is done in holy garments, after washing, on pain of death, and only by those he has chosen.

evidence.note: Levi was set apart “to carry the ark of the covenant of Yahweh, to stand before Yahweh to minister to him (לְשָׁרְתוֹ), and to bless in his name”.
“Yahweh your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand to minister in the name of Yahweh.”
“The priest who stands to minister there before Yahweh your God.”
“The priests the sons of Levi, for Yahweh your God has chosen them to minister to him and to bless in the name of Yahweh.”
The robe's bells are heard “when he goes into the holy place before Yahweh … that he not die”.
“When they draw near to the altar to minister in the holy place, that they bear no iniquity and die.”
“When they draw near to the altar to minister, to burn an offering to Yahweh, they shall wash with water, that they not die.”
“The boy was ministering to Yahweh before Eli the priest.”
“Samuel was ministering before Yahweh, a boy girded with a linen ephod.”
“The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of Yahweh filled the house.”
“Priests ministering to Yahweh, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites in their work.”
“Yahweh has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him, and to be his ministers and burn incense.”
Yahweh's covenant “with the Levites the priests, my ministers”, as sure as his covenant with David.
The sons of Zadok “shall draw near to me to minister to me, and they shall stand before me to offer to me the fat and the blood”.
“They shall draw near to my table to minister to me, and keep my charge.”
“The priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who draw near to minister to Yahweh.”
“The priests, the ministers of Yahweh, mourn.”
“Wail, ministers of the altar … ministers of my God.”
“Between the porch and the altar let the priests, the ministers of Yahweh, weep.”
To the restored people: “you shall be called priests of Yahweh; ministers of our God (מְשָׁרְתֵי אֱלֹהֵינוּ) it shall be said of you”.
“The sons of the foreigner who join themselves to Yahweh, to minister to him and to love the name of Yahweh.”
“The rams of Nebaioth shall minister to you; they shall go up with acceptance on my altar”: offerings in Zion's worship.
“Every priest stands daily ministering (λειτουργῶν)”: the standing to minister of Deu 18:7.
Zechariah the priest goes home when “the days of his ministry (λειτουργίας)” are ended.

senses.gloss: serve the tabernacle, the priests, the congregation (Levites)
senses.definition: The Levites' service: to attend to the tabernacle and its vessels, to wait on the priests, to stand before the congregation and serve it, to keep the gates, to sing, and to boil the people's sacrifices.

evidence.note: “They shall carry the tabernacle and all its vessels, and they shall minister to it (יְשָׁרְתֻהוּ), and camp around the tabernacle.”
“Bring the tribe of Levi near and set them before Aaron the priest, and they shall minister to him.”
The Levites are “joined to you and minister to you”, while Aaron and his sons are before the tent.
From fifty, the Levite “shall minister with his brothers in the tent of meeting, to keep the charge, but shall do no work”.
“To bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle of Yahweh, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them.”
“Yahweh chose them to carry the ark of Yahweh and to minister to him forever.”
The singers “were ministering before the tabernacle of the tent of meeting with song”.
The gatekeepers' divisions “to minister in the house of Yahweh”.
The Levites “to praise and to minister before the priests”.
Ezra sends for “ministers (מְשָׁרְתִים) for the house of our God”.
“They shall be ministers in my sanctuary, overseers at the gates of the house, ministering to the house; they shall slay the burnt offering … and stand before them to minister to them.”
“The Levites, the ministers of the house.”
“The kitchens, where the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people.”

senses.definition: The holy garments in which the priests minister and the vessels with which the ministry is done, named by the infinitive “for ministering” or a clause “with which they minister”.

evidence.note: “The garments of service (בִּגְדֵי הַשְּׂרָד) for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest.”
“All the vessels of the ministry (כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת) with which they minister (יְשָׁרְתוּ) in the holy place.”
The Babylonians take “all the vessels of bronze with which they ministered”.
The priests lay aside “their garments in which they minister, for they are holy”.

senses.definition: Yahweh's angels and hosts are his ministers, who stand before him and do his will.

evidence.note: “Bless Yahweh, all his hosts, his ministers (מְשָׁרְתָיו) who do his will”, after “his angels, mighty in strength, who do his word” (Psa 103:20).
“Who makes his angels winds (or spirits), his ministers a flaming fire.”
Quotes Psa 104:4: “who makes his angels spirits and his ministers (λειτουργούς) a flame of fire”.
“Are they not all ministering (λειτουργικά) spirits, sent out to serve for those who will inherit salvation?”

senses.definition: Twice of idolatry: to serve wood and stone, and the Levites' ministering to the people before their idols.

evidence.note: “We will be like the nations … to serve (לְשָׁרֵת) wood and stone.”
“Because they ministered to them before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel.”

evidence.locator: Deu.18.7, וְשֵׁרֵת → λειτουργήσει; Ezk.44.11, מְשָׁרְתִים → λειτουργοῦντες; λειτουργέω and its forms render שָׁרַת about 55 times

evidence.note: “Every priest stands daily ministering (λειτουργῶν) and offering the same sacrifices”: the priests' standing to minister of Deu 18:7, set against Christ, who has sat down (Heb 10:12).
“As they ministered (λειτουργούντων) to the Lord and fasted.”

evidence.locator: Psa.103.21, מְשָׁרְתָיו → λειτουργοί; Isa.61.6, מְשָׁרְתֵי → λειτουργοί; Neh.10.40

evidence.note: Quotes Psa 104:4, “his ministers (λειτουργούς) a flame of fire”, of the angels.
Christ, the high priest seated at the right hand, “a minister (λειτουργός) of the holy places and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man”.
Paul “a minister of Jesus Christ to the nations, ministering the good news of God as a priest”.

parallels.note: “Draw near”: the priest draws near to the altar, the table, or Yahweh himself to minister.
“Bless in his name”: the priests' other duty beside ministering.

phrases.gloss: stand before Yahweh to minister to him

words.summary: Twice, both in כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת “the vessels of the ministry”. The form is the piel infinitive used as a noun.

senses.definition: The service done in Yahweh's sanctuary, in the phrase “vessels of the ministry”, the vessels the priests and Levites used in it.

evidence.note: “All the vessels of the ministry (כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת) with which they minister in the holy place”, wrapped in blue for the journey.
With the silver left over from the repair Jehoiada had “vessels of ministry and of offering up” made for the house of Yahweh.
Moses sprinkled with blood “the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry (τῆς λειτουργίας)”.

evidence.locator: Num.4.12, כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת → σκεύη τὰ λειτουργικά; 2Ch.24.14; λειτουργικός renders שָׁרֵת ×2

evidence.note: The angels are “ministering (λειτουργικά) spirits”: the word of the ministry vessels used of the ministers of Psa 103:21 and 104:4.

cognates.gloss: (piel) serve a god and the community; render public service
cognates.note: Punic: whoever does not serve is cursed by Tinnit and Baal-Hammon, whoever serves zealously shall have wealth and peace; a mother “rendered public service for fifty years”. The same service of a god and of the people as the Hebrew's ministering to Yahweh and to the congregation (Num 16:9). Phoenician writes one letter for š and ṯ, so it cannot show which sound stands behind ש.

evidence.locator: p. 481, Š-R-T I, citing CIS i 5510.4–7 and NP 130.4

cognates.gloss: service; public service (to the community or a temple)
cognates.note: The noun šrt “service” in ʿm šrt “the service personnel” (KAI 136), and mšrt “public service”, used of a man in charge of a temple's building who was crowned by the Sidonians (KAI 60) and of restoring a sanctuary (Mactar B). Like the Hebrew שָׁרֵת, service done for a temple.

evidence.locator: p. 318, MŠRT, citing KAI 60.1–4, KAI 123.1–4, Mactar B II 2

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in Targum Pseudo-Jonathan only, in the phrase “ministering angels”: the Hebrew of the rabbis' מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת taken into Aramaic, whose own verb for “serve, minister” is שַׁמֵּשׁ (Dan 7:10). Borrowed from Hebrew, not independent evidence.

evidence.locator: s.v. שֵׁירוּתָא I (ch.), citing Targ. Y. Gen. XVIII, 20 (מלאכי ש׳ ministering angels)

doctrine.statement: The Psalm calls on Yahweh's angels, “mighty in strength, who do his word”, and in the same breath on “all his hosts, his ministers who do his will” (Psa 103:20–21); he “makes his angels spirits, his ministers a flaming fire” (Psa 104:4). The letter to the Hebrews quotes Psa 104:4 to set the angels below the Son, to whom God said “you are my Son” and “sit at my right hand”, which he never said to an angel, and concludes: “are they not all ministering spirits, sent out to serve for those who will inherit salvation?” (Heb 1:4–7, 13–14). From the verses: angels are Yahweh's servants, made by him, who stand before him and do what he commands; they are sent to serve the heirs of salvation, and are not the departed spirits of men nor rivals to God.

Under the law only those Yahweh chose might stand before him to minister, and only washed, in holy garments, “that they not die” (Deu 18:5; Exo 28:43; 30:20); their ministry was done standing, day after day, and when his glory filled the house they could not stand to minister at all (1Ki 8:11). Hebrews takes up the word: “every priest stands daily ministering and offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins; but this man, having offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down at the right hand of God” (Heb 10:11–12), and he is now “a minister of the holy places and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man” (Heb 8:1–2). From the verses: the Levitical ministry was the pattern; Jesus, raised and set at God's right hand, is the high priest whose ministry it foreshadowed, and his one offering finished what theirs repeated.

Isaiah foretells a Zion rebuilt, where “the sons of foreigners shall build your walls and their kings shall serve you”, and the rams of Nebaioth go up with acceptance on Yahweh's altar (Isa 60:7, 10); foreigners who join themselves to Yahweh “to minister to him” are brought to his holy mountain, for “my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples” (Isa 56:6–7), words Jesus quoted in the temple (Mrk 11:17). The redeemed themselves “shall be called priests of Yahweh, ministers of our God” (Isa 61:6), in the chapter whose opening Jesus read as fulfilled in himself (Luk 4:18–21). The saints in Revelation sing that he has made them “kings and priests to our God, and we shall reign on the earth” (Rev 5:10; 1:6). From the verses: the ministry once kept to one tribe is promised to all the redeemed, Jew and Gentile, as kings and priests in a kingdom on the earth, centred on Zion.

note: Words left out: BDB's שֵׁשׁ v.gg.af “byssus, fine linen” sits after this root in BDB's order but is not of it: its consonants are שש and it is borrowed from Egyptian šs (Wiktionary; the brief's TLA matches give šs “rope” and “alabaster”, not yet checked for a linen sense). The database maps all the spelling's tokens to v.gg.af, so its 167 count is mostly the numeral six (shesh.json, v.bk.ab) and the marble שֵׁשׁ (v.cw.ab, beside שַׁיִשׁ). No entry holds the linen yet; it wants its own entry (root שש, homograph of shesh, with an egy loan cognate). No personal name is formed from this root (none in TIPNR). Cognates: only Phoenician-Punic has the root (Krahmalkov, read from the OCR text: check pp. 318, 379, 481 against the page images, and the Phoenician script forms). Lane has nothing under سرت or ثرت, Oracc's šrt candidates (šarrūtu, šērtu…) are other roots, the Oracc Ugarit glossary and Segert show no šrt or ṯrt “serve”, and the Peshitta has no cognate root: Syriac and Biblical Aramaic use שַׁמֵּשׁ (Dan 7:10). So no cognate shows which sound stands behind ש, and `sounds` is empty; look for Ugaritic in DULAT and for Old South Arabic. Jastrow's שָׁרַת and שָׁרֵת are Mishnaic Hebrew, not Aramaic, and his “[to dwell with]” etymology is a lead not followed. Verse numbering is the Hebrew's: 1Ch 6:17 is English 6:32, Neh 10:37 and 10:40 are English 10:36 and 10:39. MACULA has no alignment for מְשָׁרְתָיו in Psa 104:4 (the LXX there is λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ), so it is not in the λειτουργός locator. Open question: whether the Levites' service (levites-serve) and the garments and vessels sense should be narrower senses of minister-yahweh.
